body:
## Status and adopted direction

Target: **Qleisli 0.3.0 type-system specification**.

**User decision, 2026-10-02:** remove the classical `C` type prefix from the surface model. Classical/ordinary data is the unmarked baseline; `Q<T>` is the quantum ownership constructor.

In particular, the intended 0.3.0 direction is:

```text
CBit       -> Bit
CBits<n>   -> Bits<n>
C<T>       -> T        // do not introduce a general classical modality
```

while quantum data remains explicit:

```text
Bit        ordinary/classical bit
Bits<n>    ordinary/classical finite bit sequence

Q<Bit>     quantum ownership with basis Bit
Q<Bits<n>> quantum ownership with basis Bits<n>
```

This supersedes the earlier framing of this issue as merely “two copies of the same finite set”. The stronger principle is:

> **Classical is not a modality in Qleisli. Quantum is.**

Related:
- #196 — three-level surface boundary: `q***`, `Q<T>`, unmarked syntax
- #195 — `qmatch`
- #194 — `qfor`
- #43 — `Unit` / `Q<Unit>`
- #23 — basis-state preparation
- #27 — type-theory synthesis

## Problem

The current surface model contains parallel classical and basis/quantum-facing names:

```text
Bit       vs CBit
Bits<n>   vs CBits<n>
```

and earlier design discussion left open the possibility of a general `C<T>`.

That duplicates the ordinary finite data universe even though the actual semantic distinction is already represented by `Q<T>`.

A measured bit is not “a bit in a second classical modality”. It is simply an ordinary `Bit`.

Likewise, a coherent bit is not another kind of `Bit`; it is quantum ownership over the same finite basis:

```text
Q<Bit>
```

The old naming therefore places the quantum/classical boundary in the wrong location.

## Three-level surface model

This issue is the type-level part of #196.

Qleisli should expose three cases:

### 1. Unmarked ordinary values

```qli
b: Bit
word: Bits<n>
n: Nat
()```

These are ordinary copyable/droppable classical or static values, subject to their normal staging rules.

### 2. Quantum-owned values

```qli
q: Q<Bit>
register: Q<Bits<n>>
```

The `Q<...>` constructor is what changes ownership, coherence, observation and resource rules.

### 3. Dedicated `q***` constructs where the construct itself changes meaning

Examples:

```text
if      / qif
for     / qfor
match   / qmatch
```

Do not encode the same boundary a second time with `CBit`, `CBits` or `C<T>`.

## Consequence for observation

The natural observation signatures become:

```text
measure_z    : Q<Bit>     -> Bit
measure_bits : Q<Bits<n>> -> Bits<n>
```

The type transition itself says exactly what happened:

```text
Q<T> -> T
```

together with the declared `Observe` effect.

No `C` wrapper is needed to mark the result as classical.

This does **not** make observation implicit. There remains no coercion:

```text
Q<T> -> T
```

except through an operation whose semantics/effect explicitly permits observation.

## Consequence for control flow

The distinction becomes direct:

```text
b : Bit
if b { ... }                 // ordinary classical branch

q : Q<Bit>
qif(q, target) { ... }       // coherent quantum control
```

and similarly:

```text
Bits<n>       -> match
Q<Bits<n>>    -> qmatch when coherent basis-space control is intended
```

This is the intended interaction between unmarked types, `Q<T>`, and the `q***` family.

## One finite type universe

The preferred conceptual model is one ordinary finite data/basis grammar, for example:

```text
A ::= Unit | Bit | Bits<n> | A × B | ...
```

with:

```text
A       ordinary value of A
Q<A>    linear quantum ownership whose computational basis is A
```

“Basis type” therefore describes the role of `A` under `Q<A>`; it need not be a second source-level copy of the same finite set.

Static/basis computation and runtime classical computation may still have different **judgments, staging rules or admissible operations**. Those distinctions belong in typing/staging, not in a duplicate `C...` type family.

## Basis/static reuse

A total finite function should be reusable where its semantics permits:

```text
f : A -> B
```

may serve:

- ordinary classical computation;
- compile-time/static evaluation;
- checked coherent lifting when Qleisli can prove the required totality/injectivity/semantic conditions.

The language must not duplicate the function merely because the same finite map is used before and after measurement.

This does not permit coherent data to be read classically.

## Literal spelling

0.3.0 should choose one coherent literal story for the unified finite type.

The important semantic decision in this issue is the **single type**, not whether the preferred surface literals are `0/1`, `false/true`, or a narrowly specified aliasing policy.

Whichever spelling is adopted:

- it must not recreate `Bit` vs `CBit` through literal classes;
- coherent basis labels and ordinary values denote elements of the same `Bit` type;
- access to a value inside `Q<Bit>` still requires quantum semantics, not ordinary evaluation.

## Migration

This is a breaking 0.3.0 surface migration.

At minimum audit and migrate:

- `CBit` -> `Bit`;
- `CBits<n>` -> `Bits<n>`;
- measurement/readout signatures;
- classical Boolean operators and branch guards;
- sized QPE/readout corpus;
- AST and parser variants;
- Rust/Lean public type representations where externally visible;
- IR/interchange schema names where they encode the old source distinction;
- docs, examples, diagnostics and authoring corpus;
- any planned `C<T>` abstraction: remove it from the design unless a distinct future semantic need is demonstrated.

Internal verifier representations may remain distinct where staging or port classification genuinely requires it, but that distinction must not leak back into duplicate source types without a separate semantic justification.

## Obligations

- No implicit readout of `Q<A>`.
- `Q<A>` remains linear and cannot be copied or implicitly discarded.
- Ordinary `A` remains unrestricted where the ordinary type permits it.
- `Observe` remains an explicit effect boundary.
- `if` and `qif` remain semantically distinct.
- `match` and `qmatch` remain semantically distinct.
- No hidden coercion from `Q<A>` to `A`.
- Exact axis/bit order for `Bits<n>` remains specified.
- The migration must preserve verified quantum IR/meaning modulo the deliberate source-type rename/unification.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The Language Reference states: **ordinary/classical types are unmarked; quantum ownership is `Q<T>`.**
2. `CBit`, `CBits<n>`, and a general surface `C<T>` are absent from the adopted 0.3.0 type model.
3. Measurement examples type as `Q<Bit> -> Bit` and `Q<Bits<n>> -> Bits<n>`.
4. Classical control consumes ordinary `Bit`; coherent control consumes/preserves `Q<Bit>`.
5. One finite predicate/decoder can be reused classically and in checked coherent/static contexts when its typing obligations permit.
6. Every path that attempts to inspect `Q<A>` as ordinary `A` without an explicit permitted operation is rejected.
7. Sized QPE and measured-client examples migrate from `CBits<m>` to `Bits<m>`.
8. Diagnostics no longer teach a parallel “C-type universe”.
9. #43's `Unit` / `Q<Unit>` model is consistent with the same generic `T` / `Q<T>` rule.
10. First-attempt authoring tests verify that an LLM given a few examples infers `Bit` vs `Q<Bit>` without inventing `CBit`.

## Design principle

> **The ordinary world is the default world. `Q` marks the semantic lift into quantum ownership.**

Equivalently:

```text
T       ordinary/classical
Q<T>    quantum-owned
```

not:

```text
C<T>    classical
Q<T>    quantum
```

This keeps the type boundary aligned with Qleisli's surface boundary in #196.

## 2026-10-04 target type contract

Select `0` / `1` as the ordinary and basis Bit literals, with explicit migration from `false` / `true`. The same static-Nat numeral spelling is distinguished by its checked category. Removing `CBit` / `CBits<n>` follows the already adopted ordinary `T` / owned `Q<T>` boundary; it does not create preparation or observation coercions.

The [target Language Reference](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/reference/type-model.md) and [foundation analysis](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/design/type-foundation.md) record this ordinary implementation decision under the approved 0.3.0 plan and adopted authority hierarchy. Edition remains 2026. This is not a new Guardian interpretation or guarantee admission.

Status: target rules selected; implementation and conformance remain in progress in #307. Current alpha syntax still contains CBit/CBits and general Basis polymorphism is not yet implemented. Required positive and negative tests, exact lowering/interface preservation and native acceptance evidence remain open. Documentation alone does not complete this issue.
title: 0.3.0: remove `CBit` / `CBits` — classical data is unmarked, quantum ownership is `Q<T>`
